blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — fosfomycin administration teaching
stem: An adult woman with acute uncomplicated cystitis is prescribed fosfomycin tromethamine granules for oral solution. Which teaching by the nurse is correct?

options.A: Dissolve the full contents of the single-dose sachet in 3 to 4 ounces of water, stir, and drink it promptly as the prescribed one-dose treatment for the episode.
options.B: Take one sachet each day until urinary symptoms resolve because repeated daily dosing improves eradication and reduces adverse effects compared with a single dose.
options.C: Swallow the granules dry with a small sip of water because dissolving the sachet before administration decreases oral absorption and reduces antibacterial activity.
options.D: Save part of the sachet for a second dose the next day because the packet is intended to be divided when symptoms persist after the first administration.

rationale: Current fosfomycin tromethamine labeling states that for women 18 years and older with acute uncomplicated cystitis, the recommended dosage is one sachet. The entire sachet is dissolved in 3 to 4 ounces of water, stirred, and taken immediately; it should not be swallowed dry. The label specifically states not to use more than one single dose for a single episode because repeated daily dosing did not improve clinical or microbiologic outcomes and increased adverse events. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Teach correct oral fosfomycin administration for acute uncomplicated cystitis: one complete sachet dissolved in water and taken as a single dose, not repeated daily or swallowed dry.
source_document_title: FOSFOMYCIN TROMETHAMINE granules for oral solution — Prescribing Information
source_locator: Dosage and Administration: one sachet for women ≥18 with acute uncomplicated cystitis; do not take dry. Preparation: dissolve entire sachet in 3-4 oz water and take immediately. General Precautions: do not use more than one single dose for one episode; repeated daily doses did not improve outcomes and increased adverse events.
source_claim_supported: One sachet dissolved in water and taken immediately is the labeled regimen for acute uncomplicated cystitis; repeated daily dosing for the same episode is not recommended.

candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all choices as complete administration instructions of comparable length.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches the current April 2026 label; no absolute-word cue or second defensible administration plan remains.
